messages:
julia_sales: Hey team — ACME POC is hitting a bunch of 429s during their final load run. Sales rep just got panicked call. Can someone triage? They said it started ~10:15 PT and is blocking demo tomorrow.

sam_se: thanks for the ping. do we have the exact request id or sample headers from their client? 429s could be per-tenant token budget or per-route cap.

acme_sre: attaching the earliest curl log we captured: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 8\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 600\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-Request-ID: req_01F2A3B4\n```
We were sending batched embeddings + chat concurrently.

mateo_eng_oncall: @sam_se @julia_sales looking... that X-RateLimit-Limit is odd for the tenant. can you paste the route name used? is it /v1/chat or /v1/embeddings?

acme_sre: main flows: `/v1/chat/completions` (concurrent streaming) and `/v1/embeddings` in parallel. Client used 16 concurrent streams, batch size 8 for embeddings.

sam_se: ok two things to check in parallel: 1) per-route cap (sales quota config can set tighter per-route caps), 2) token budget for the trial tenant (we throttle once tokens/day is exceeded). @olivia_billing can you confirm their token budget?

olivia_billing: pulling it now — ACME trial account has a 500k token day budget and a per-route soft-cap of 600 rps for chat that we historically set for trial tiers. usage spike shows they burned ~420k tokens in the first 30m.

mateo_eng_oncall: that lines up — chat + embeddings parallelized will blow token budget fast. The X-RateLimit-Limit 600 looks like the per-route rps cap. 16 streams x avg 1.2rps each ~19rps, but embeddings batch expansion can multiply tokens. Need exact token accounting.

julia_sales: customer says they were only doing a single scripted demo load (no runaway test). Can we do a temporary bump for tomorrow's demo? even +2x would help.

sam_se: two paths: a) quick emergency quota bump (manual, low risk) from sales/billing for demo window, b) recommend client to reduce concurrency and enable client-side backoff. I'll draft conservative guidance: reduce embeddings batch to 4, limit concurrency to 6, exponential backoff on 429 with jitter.

mateo_eng_oncall: I can enable a temporary per-route override for the tenant for a 2 hour window. Need approval from billing for chargeable bump and confirmation of exact window. Also will add a temporary rule to treat 429 Retry-After header to backpressure clients.

olivia_billing: we can approve a trial-friendly temporary bump with a preauth for overage up to $200 for the demo. julia, get written consent from ACME to bill any overage, please.

julia_sales: ACME gave verbal OK; sending them the note now for written consent.

acme_sre: quick Q — do you have an internal link to see per-route token accounting? would help debug client behavior.

sam_se: yes, Console -> Usage -> Per-Route shows token and rps. I’m pulling the dashboard now and will paste the last 1h graph.

sam_se: pasted: (chart) chat tokens spike to 260k between 10:05-10:20, embeddings ~180k same window.

mateo_eng_oncall: that's the smoking gun. Also saw many 429s with Retry-After: 8 which means client retried quickly and then retried again — creating retry storms. We'll add a guard on our gateway to honor and enforce Retry-After and add jitter for the next deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy queued — gateway-ratebackpressure @mateo_eng_oncall requested. CI pipeline #4821, ETA ~18 minutes.

olivia_billing: once we flip the temporary increase, billing will flag it as an approved demo bump. I'll set a hard cap of $200 and notify finance.

julia_sales: ACME signed consent via email at 10:30 PT. Copying text: "we authorize Redwood to temporarily increase quotas for our trial for the demo window and accept any charges up to $200."

mateo_eng_oncall: thanks. I'm toggling per-route override: chat cap 600 -> 1200 rps for tenant acme-prod for 2 hours starting 10:45 PT. Also added temporary token buffer.

acme_sre: confirming 10:46 — demo is progressing, 429s dropped by ~95%. Latency a bit higher but acceptable.

sam_se: sent recommended client-side changes to ACME engineer: reduce embeddings batch size to 4, concurrency <= 6, apply exponential backoff with cap 60s, and respect Retry-After. Also suggested enabling KV prefix caching for repeated prompts.

mateo_eng_oncall: follow-up ops: we'll keep the override until 12:45 PT then auto-revert. I'll leave a 30m pre-revert notice in this thread. Also enabling extra request logging for that tenant while override active (request ids + route keys).

olivia_billing: billing note: if usage exceeds $200 we'll suspend further requests and notify accounts.

julia_sales: ACME says demo passed, team is happy. thanks everyone for the quick help. :clap:

mateo_eng_oncall: 12:15 PT — 30m warning: preparing to revert per-route override at 12:45 PT. Any objections?

acme_sre: no objections. we'll throttle client to the original profile before revert.

mateo_eng_oncall: 12:46 PT — override reverted automatically. All caps back to baseline.

sam_se: marking this POC follow-up: create a best-practice note for trial customers: recommended concurrency/batch defaults and sample backoff code. Also add a short-blurb on per-route caps visibility.

julia_sales: will follow up with ACME this week about upgrade options so they don't hit this in prod.

acme_sre: thanks again, team. saved the export of logs and req_01F2A3B4 for postmortem.

mateo_eng_oncall: closing thread, moving notes into the runbook. :white_check_mark:
